content: The hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 plays a critical role in the metabolism of many drugs. Below are detailed interactions and recommendations for specific drugs when co-administered with ritonavir or lopinavir: 1. Triptorelin and Lopinavir: Triptorelin increases the toxicity of lopinavir by prolonging the QTc interval, raising the risk of torsades de pointes. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 2. Ritonavir and Tucatinib: Ritonavir increases tucatinib levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Tucatinib also increases lopinavir levels via the same mechanism, necessitating similar caution. 3. Tucatinib and CYP3A Substrates: Avoid co-administration of tucatinib with CYP3A substrates where even minimal concentration changes could lead to severe or life-threatening toxicities. If unavoidable, reduce the dose of the CYP3A substrate as per product labeling. 4. Lopinavir and Ulipristal: Lopinavir increases ulipristal levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 5. Vemurafenib and Ritonavir/Lopinavir: Both drugs increase the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Ritonavir and lopinavir also increase vemurafenib levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. 6. Lopinavir and Verapamil: Lopinavir increases verapamil levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 7. Lopinavir and Vilanterol/Fluticasone: Lopinavir increases the toxicity of this combination by prolonging the QTc interval. Extreme caution is advised when co-administering vilanterol with drugs that prolong the QTc interval, as adrenergic agonist effects on the cardiovascular system may be potentiated. 8. Ritonavir and Vilazodone: Ritonavir increases vilazodone levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase vilazodone plasma levels by 50%, requiring a dose reduction to 20 mg daily. 9. Lopinavir and Vinblastine/Vincristine: Lopinavir increases the levels of vinblastine and vincristine by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 10. Ritonavir and Vorapaxar: Ritonavir increases vorapaxar levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 11. Ritonavir and Voriconazole: Ritonavir increases voriconazole levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 12. Ritonavir and Vortioxetine: Ritonavir increases vortioxetine levels by affecting CYP2D6 metabolism. Reduce the vortioxetine dose by 50% when co-administered with strong CYP2D6 inhibitors. 13. Ritonavir and Abacavir: Both drugs increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Use caution and monitor closely. 14. Lopinavir and Abemaciclib: Lopinavir increases abemaciclib levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Dose reduction of abemaciclib is required when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 15. Lopinavir and Acarbose: Lopinavir decreases the effects of acarbose through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor closely. 16. Ritonavir and Albiglutide: Ritonavir decreases the effects of albiglutide, potentially due to insulin resistance. Use caution and monitor closely. 17. Lopinavir and Alfuzosin: Both drugs increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 18. Ritonavir and Alprazolam: Ritonavir increases alprazolam levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 19. Ritonavir and Amikacin: Ritonavir increases amikacin levels via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 20. Ritonavir and Amitriptyline: Ritonavir increases amitriptyline levels via CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 21. Lopinavir and Amlodipine: Lopinavir increases amlodipine levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 22. Amobarbital and Ritonavir/Lopinavir: Amobarbital decreases ritonavir and lopinavir levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 23. Ritonavir and Apalutamide: Ritonavir increases apalutamide levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 24. Lopinavir and Apixaban: Lopinavir increases apixaban levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 25. Ritonavir and Atorvastatin: Ritonavir increases atorvastatin levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 26. Azithromycin and Lopinavir: Azithromycin increases lopinavir toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 27. Ritonavir and Bazedoxifene/Conjugated Estrogens: Ritonavir affects the metabolism of these drugs via CYP3A4 and P-glycoprotein, potentially increasing or decreasing their levels. Use caution and monitor closely. 28. Lopinavir and Bedaquiline: Both drugs increase the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor closely, including ECG monitoring. 29. Ritonavir and Benzhydrocodone/Acetaminophen: Ritonavir increases hydrocodone levels (a prodrug of benzhydrocodone) via CYP3A4 metabolism, potentially leading to fatal respiratory depression. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 30. Ritonavir and Brexpiprazole: Ritonavir increases brexpiprazole levels via CYP3A4 and CYP2D6 metabolism. Administer half the usual dose of brexpiprazole when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 or CYP2D6 inhibitors. 31. Ritonavir and Bromocriptine: Ritonavir increases bromocriptine levels by decreasing metabolism, likely due to CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 32. Ritonavir and Buprenorphine: Ritonavir increases buprenorphine levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, potentially leading to increased toxicity. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 33. Ritonavir and Bupropion: Ritonavir decreases bupropion levels by inducing CYP2B6 metabolism. Dose adjustments of bupropion may be required. 34. Ritonavir and Buspirone: Ritonavir increases buspirone levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 35. Ritonavir and Cabazitaxel: Ritonavir increases cabazitaxel levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, increasing the risk of toxicity. Avoid co-administration. 36. Ritonavir and Cannabidiol: Ritonavir increases cannabidiol levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Consider reducing the cannabidiol dose when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 37. Ritonavir and Cariprazine: Ritonavir increases cariprazine levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Dose reduction of cariprazine is required when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 38. Ritonavir and Carvedilol: Ritonavir increases carvedilol levels via CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 39. Ritonavir and Cetirizine: Ritonavir increases cetirizine levels by decreasing metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 40. Ritonavir and Cholic Acid: Ritonavir decreases cholic acid elimination, potentially exacerbating bile salt accumulation in the liver. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 41. Ritonavir and Chlordiazepoxide: Ritonavir increases chlordiazepoxide levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Consider lowering the benzodiazepine dose or using alternatives. 42. Ritonavir and Chloroquine: Chloroquine increases lopinavir toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 43. Ritonavir and Cabozantinib: Ritonavir increases cabozantinib levels, potentially increasing toxicity. Use caution and monitor closely. 44. Ritonavir and Canagliflozin: Ritonavir decreases canagliflozin levels by increasing metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 45. Ritonavir and Capmatinib: Ritonavir increases capmatinib levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 46. Ritonavir and Cariprazine: Ritonavir increases cariprazine levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Dose reduction is required when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 47. Ritonavir and Brexpiprazole: Ritonavir increases brexpiprazole levels via CYP3A4 and CYP2D6 metabolism. Adjust brexpiprazole dose accordingly. 48. Ritonavir and Buprenorphine (Various Forms): Ritonavir increases buprenorphine levels across different formulations (e.g., buccal, subdermal implant, long-acting injection) via CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor for signs of toxicity or overdose and adjust therapy as needed. 49. Ritonavir and Bupropion: Ritonavir decreases bupropion levels by inducing CYP2B6 metabolism. Increased doses of bupropion may be required. 50. Ritonavir and Butabarbital/Butalbital: These drugs decrease ritonavir and lopinavir levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 51. Ritonavir and Cabazitaxel: Ritonavir increases cabazitaxel levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, increasing the risk of toxicity. Avoid co-administration. 52. Ritonavir and Calcifediol: Ritonavir affects vitamin D metabolism, potentially altering serum calcifediol levels. Dose adjustment and close monitoring of vitamin D, PTH, and calcium levels are recommended. 53. Ritonavir and Cannabidiol: Ritonavir increases cannabidiol levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Consider reducing the cannabidiol dose when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 54. Ritonavir and Cariprazine: Ritonavir increases cariprazine levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Dose reduction is required when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 55. Ritonavir and Cetirizine: Ritonavir increases cetirizine levels by decreasing metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 56. Ritonavir and Chlordiazepoxide: Ritonavir increases chlordiazepoxide levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Consider lowering the benzodiazepine dose or using alternatives. 57. Ritonavir and Cholic Acid: Ritonavir decreases cholic acid elimination, potentially exacerbating bile salt accumulation in the liver. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 58. Ritonavir and Chloroquine: Chloroquine increases lopinavir toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely.
